1. Scope— Covers the essential dimensional, functional and quality characteristics and methods of 
testing the accuracy of vernier height gauges with least count 0*02 mm and a maximum measuring 
range of 1 000 mm. 

2. Nomenclature — See Fig. 1. 

3. Definitions 

3.1 Error of Measurement — Ihe algebraic difference between the measured size and the true 
size. 

3.2 Measuring Rar)ge — The maximum height which can be measured by moving the sliding jaw 
vertically upwards from the base. 

3.3 Measur/nflf t//?cer/a/7j/y — The error margin corresponding to the inherent errors of measure- 
ment of vernier height gauge. It is defined as being equal to ± 2 s, that is, for a normal distribution 
of the readings on the instrument, about 95% of readings will not deviate from the mean size 
( true value ) by more than twice the standard deviation(s). 

4. Measuring Range — The recommended measuring ranges are 250, 300, 500, 750 and 1 000 mm. 

5. IMaterial — The main parts of vernier height gauges such as beam, sliding jaw clamp, scriber 
and mearuring jaw shall be manufactured from either plain carbon steel or stainless steel with a 
coefficient of thermal expansion in the temperature range 10 to 30°C within the ilimits (11*5 ± I'O) 
X 10-«°C-i. 

6. Hardness — The hardness shall not be less than 550 HV for the measuring jaw and not less 
than 700 HV for the scriber. 

7. General Requirements 

7.1 Base 

7.1.1 The base shall be of ample proportions to ensure rigidity and stability of the gauge. It 
shall be relieved on the underside leaving a surface round the outside edge, at least 12 mm wide 
and shall have air groove across this surface to connect the relieved part with the outside. 

7.1.2, The base shall be ground and lapped to within flatness error 0'005 mm as measured over 
the total span of the surface considered. 

7.2 Beam 

7.2.1 The section of the beam shall be such as to ensure rigidity during use. 

7.2.2 The guiding edge of the beam shall be flat within tolerance shown in col 2 of of Table 1. 
This edge shall also be square to the base within O'OS mm/100 mm. 

7.2.3 The faces of the beam shall b 3 flat within tolerance shown in col 3 of Table 1. These faces 
shall also be square to the base within 0*04 mm/100 mm.

7.3 Measuring Jaw and Scriber 

7.3.1 The clear projection of the measuring jaw from the edge of the beam shall be at least 
equal to the projection of the base from the beam. For all positions of the slider, the upper and 
lower gauging surfaces of the measuring jaw shal! be flat and parallel to the base to within 
022 mm/iOO mm height* This measurement should be done over the area at a maximum distance 
of 25 mm from the beam, otherwise necessary correction factor should be applied to observed 
readings according to the distance. 

7=3=2 The projection of the scriber beyond the jaw shall be at least 25 mm. Vernier height 
gauges may have an offset scriber and the scale on the beam so positioned that when the scriber 
is co-plane with the base, the vernier is at zero position. 

7.3.3 The measuring faces of the scriber shall be flat and parallel to within 0*005 mm. 
8. Graduations 

8.1 All graduations shall be clearly engraved. The thickness of graduations shall be not less than 
08 mm nor more than 018 mm and shall not differ by more than 003 mm. 

8.2 The visible length of the shortest graduations ( dimension W in Fig. 2 ) shall not be less than 
three times the width of the interval between the adjacent lines. 

8.2.1 The perpendicular distance from the graduated face of the beam to the graduated bevell- 
ed face of the vernier ( dimension Tin Fig. 2 ) shall not exceed 0*10 mm.

8.3 To facilitate reading, the surfaces of the beam and the vernier may be given a matt finish and 
the graduation lines filled with black pigment. 

9. Accuracy 

9.1 Meastfr/ny Error — The permissible measuring error in micrometres as given In Table 2. is 
calculated from the following formula: 

e === ± ( 20 -I- 0-05 L ) 

where e is the measuring error in micrometres (ftm) and L is any measured length In milli- 
metres within the measuring range. The calculated values shall be rounded off to the nearest 
10 /xm. 

Not< — For convenience, the definitive values appropriate to a specific measured length (I) are oiven in 
Table 2.

9.2 The recommended method of test to check measuring error Is given in Appendix A. 

10. Designation — The vernier height gauge shall be designated by the measuring range, least 
count, the material used and number of this standard. 

Example 

A vernier height gauge with a measuring range of 250 mm. least count 002 mm and 
made of stainless steel shall be designated as: 

Vernier Height Gauge 250-0*02 Stainless Steel IS : 2921 

11. Marking — Vernier height gauge shall be legibly and permanently marked in characters not 
less than 1 mm high with: 

a) the unit symbol of the scale figures on the beam ( millimetre or centimetre ), 

b) the name of the manufacturer or his trade mark on the beam, and 

c) the indication 1/50 mm or 0'C2 mm on the vernier. 

11.1 Standard Marking — Details available with the Bureau of Indian Standards. 

12. Packing — Each vernier height gauge shall be packed in suitable anticorrosive packing mate- 
rial. The height gauge shall then be supplied in a suitable protective case. 



APPENDIX A 

( Clause 9.2 ) 

METHOD OF TEST TO CHECK MEASURING UNCERTAINTY 

A-1. It is recommended that the measuring error be checked at the standard temperature given in 
IS ; 7018 ( Part 1 )-1983 'Technical supply conditions for gauges : Part 1 General*. The test is 
carried out by setting the height gauge with combinations of slip gauges having a precision at 
least equal to Grade 2 ( see IS : 2984-1981 'Specification for slip gauges)'. The sizes of slip gauge 
combinations shall be chosen to cover a number of positions over the measuring range of the 
instrument including the vernier scale. 

A-1.1 Each slip gauge combination shall be placed between the scriber and the surface plate in 
at least three positions along the length of the measuring face of the scriber. The reading shall 
be noted at each position and compared with the size of the slip gauges. 

A-2. The thickness of the scale lines may be checked by direct measurement with a microscope 
fitted with a micrometric device or by a measuring machine. 



IS : 2921 - 1988 

E X P L A N A T O R Y NOTE 

This standard was originally published in 1964 based on BS 1643 : 1950 'Vernier height 
gauges', issued by the British Standards Institution ( BSI ), 

This first revision has been brought out based on the prevailing manufacturing practices jn 
India and to bring about similarity in terminology and related requirements given in ISO standards 
on vernier calipers. 

Some of the main changes made are given below: 

a) Fig. 1 has been modified to include main scale adjustment mechanism ( optional ) and fine 
adjustment mechanism, 

b) A clause on terminology has been added, 

c) A clause on hardness has been added, 

d) The clause on material has been modified to include coefficient of thermal expansion of 
material, and 

e) Standard has been restructured and Tables 1 and 2 on permissible errors have also been 
modified. Unnecessary measuring parameters have been deleted. 



Reprography Unit, BIS, New Delhi, [ndi
